label: rem:flavor-charge-assignments
title: Flavor charge assignments and the hypercharge gap
html:
The A_2 weight lattice of the A_2 proposition assigns two quantum numbers to each state: the third component of isospin I_3 and the hypercharge Y, related to the fundamental weights by

  I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2),
  \qquad
  Y   = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2).

The electric charge is then the Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation Q = I_3 + Y/2.

Derived quantity: isospin I_3. The writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 is derived in the framework without fitted parameters. Over the nucleon doublet, the proton braid \mathfrak{p} and neutron braid \mathfrak{n} carry writhes whose difference reproduces \Delta I_3 = 1 scale-free. This identifies I_3 as the writhe coordinate on the A_2 weight lattice. These writhes are those of the inter-nucleon arc, w(\mathfrak{p}) = +1 and w(\mathfrak{n}) = -1. The ruled nucleon word (\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}^{-1})^3 is the same for both nucleons and has writhe 0, so on the word itself the writhe does not separate them; there I_3 is the weight of the up and down strand labels.

Open quantity: hypercharge Y. The proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ. This falsifies every injective map from the writhe to Y, in particular the linear map Y = c\,w that a framing phase q^{w c} would give. It does not falsify every function of the writhe: a non-injective one such as Y = w^2/4 passes the proton–neutron test. What does force a second invariant is the charge side. The quark charges are not a function of the writhe (the anti-up and down crossings share the writhe -1 but carry -\tfrac{2}{3} and -\tfrac{1}{3}; see the Coulomb-charge definition), and if both Q and I_3 were functions of the writhe then so would be Y = 2(Q - I_3). Since I_3 is read here as the writhe coordinate, a hypercharge independent of the writhe requires a charge Q that is not the halved writhe. The framework therefore requires a second invariant, independent of the writhe, to instantiate Y.

The candidate direction, recorded without endorsement, is the ribbon-framing twist. In the categorical braid representation, each strand carries a framing datum whose total T(t) is independent of the crossing word (hence independent of the writhe w). The candidate hypercharge is

  Y_t = 2\bigl(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3\bigr),
  \qquad
  Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = \frac{T(t)}{3},

where T(t)/3 is the colour-tube charge quantum of the quark picture (the helon-model normalisation of Sundance O. Bilson-Thompson [bilson-thompson2005]; in the braided-ribbon-graph formulation of Sundance O. Bilson-Thompson, Fotini Markopoulou, and Lee Smolin [bilsonthompson2007, §I, §V], strand twists define noiseless U(1)-charged subsystems conserved under local evolution moves, without claiming to derive the Standard Model interactions). The Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation holds by construction if and only if Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q against an independently derived electric charge Q --- a falsifiable consistency condition. The halved writhe of the Coulomb-charge definition cannot play that role, since it is not the electric charge, so the condition has no derived right-hand side yet.

Status and batteries. Neither the candidate nor any alternative has been wired. Any hypercharge proposal must pass two batteries before instantiating the class:

  1. Gell-Mann--Nishijima consistency: Q = I_3 + Y/2 must hold against an independently derived Q and I_3 on the nucleon doublet, without tuning a coupling. No derived Q exists yet, so this battery cannot currently be run against anything but the Standard-Model table.
  2. First-generation spectrum: The Y values of u, d, e^-, \nu_e must reproduce \{+1/3, +1/3, -1, -1\} (left-handed) and \{+4/3, -2/3, -2, 0\} (right-handed), satisfying the \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility relations of John C. Baez and John Huerta [baez-huerta2010].

A candidate requiring a fitted scale to pass either battery is a fit, not a derivation, and does not instantiate this class.

Enumeration result, and why it carries no corroboration. The battery has been run over all 10{,}000 helon-style assignments (3 strands per fermion, per-strand twist in \{-1, 0, +1\}), of which 4 survive. That ratio must not be read as a 2500\!:\!1 filter: the battery collapses to a single linear equation per flavour, and the surviving count is multiset counting. The following are proved:

  1. The spectrum battery is exactly T = 3Q. Both the candidate Y_t = 2(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3) and the target Y = 2(Q - I_3) carry the same -2I_3, which cancels. What remains is Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q --- the defining equation of Q_{\mathrm{twist}}, not a test of it. The battery constrains nothing about isospin.
  2. The nucleon-doublet check is entailed, by charge additivity alone: T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2T_u + T_d = 3(2Q_u + Q_d) follows from T = 3Q on the quarks, so no surviving assignment can fail it. As implemented it also states one condition twice --- its second clause 2(T_{\mathfrak{p}}/3 - 1/2) = 1 clears to T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 3, which is its own first clause.
  3. The \mathbb{Z}_6 condition is not a filter. As implemented it is a function of the Standard-Model table alone and never sees the candidate assignment; it runs as an input assertion and cannot exclude any multiset.

So each flavour is filtered independently by one equation, and 4 = 1 \times 2 \times 2 \times 1 counts the multisets of three twists from \{-1,0,+1\} with the required totals 3Q = (2, -1, 0, -3). The u-quark twist \{0,1,1\} and the electron twist \{-1,-1,-1\} are the two totals admitting a single multiset --- a fact about writing 2 and -3 as a sum of three elements of \{-1,0,+1\}, not about the framework; the d-quark and neutrino each admit two. Passing the battery is therefore equivalent to choosing t with \sum_i t_i = 3Q, which is always possible.

The open content is unchanged and is the whole question: whether the twist multisets are forced by the framework's braid words rather than only consistent with them.

A derived-twist repair, tested and refuted (scope-(a)). The defect above is that t is a free label. The natural repair is to replace it with the canonical twist of the ribbon category --- on a simple object the twist acts by a scalar whose exponent is the content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i), a derived per-block integer. Taking Q = c(\lambda)/3 is parameter-free. It does not work: at n = 3 the content sums are \{3, 0, -3\}, giving the integer charges \{+1, 0, -1\} with no third-integer charge at all, and no n \le 8 yields both quark charges \{+2/3, -1/3\} . This is scope-(a) for the plain content-sum reading, not an exclusion of the ribbon route: other normalisations remain untested.

What the hypercharge must supply for a Coulomb term. On the nucleon doublet lepton number vanishes, so the Gell-Mann--Nishijima hypercharge equals the baryon number, Y = B = 1 for both proton and neutron. Per strand this is B = \tfrac{1}{3}, and the strand charge Q = T_3 + B/2 gives u \mapsto \tfrac{2}{3}, d \mapsto -\tfrac{1}{3} and a three-strand block with a up strands the charge a - 1. So on the baryon sector the content of Y is a derived reading of B; the non-strange identification Y = B with the Milnor triple linking number of the three colour tubes is a conjecture with no instance, and the lepton sector further needs a lepton number for Y = B - L.

Hypercharge alone does not give a Coulomb pair term. The exchange of the unbroken neutral bosons between two particles has charge factor g^2\,T_3T_3' + g'^2\,(Y/2)(Y'/2), with no T_3 \otimes Y cross term. On two three-quark blocks (Y = 1, T_3 = \pm\tfrac{1}{2}) it takes the same value on the proton pair and the neutron pair: it is an isospin coupling with no Coulomb part. It splits identically as

  g^2\,T_3T_3' + g'^2\,\tfrac{Y}{2}\tfrac{Y'}{2}
  = e^2\,QQ' + g_Z^2\,(T_3 - s^2 Q)(T_3' - s^2 Q'),

with e^2 = g^2g'^2/(g^2+g'^2), s^2 = g'^2/(g^2+g'^2) and g_Z^2 = g^2+g'^2. The first term is the Coulomb factor, zero whenever a neutron is involved. On nucleon blocks the exchange with a fraction \lambda of the second term kept has the Coulomb form if and only if \lambda = 0, and the remaining coefficient e^2 vanishes exactly when g'^2 = 0. Coulomb is therefore the unbroken W^3 + B exchange minus the Z exchange, and it needs, besides Y: the mixing s^2 = \sin^2\theta_W, and a Z mass scale that removes the second term at nuclear distance. Neither is derived in this framework: the electroweak torus-link triplet of the electroweak conjecture orders m_W < m_Z < m_H by crossing number but fixes no absolute scale.

Split-bundle framing F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* and conditional hypercharge coupling. In the Standard Model appendix, the missing hypercharge and the missing three-dimensional partner are shown to be one conditional gap rather than two independent knobs. If the two-dimensional fibre V_2 (z_2 = q^3/(q^2+1)) is paired with a three-dimensional partner W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q = q^5/(q^4+q^2+1), separated from z_2 by the identity z_2 - z_3 = q^3 / ((q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)) \neq 0) inside F = V_2 \oplus W_3^*, then over any field of characteristic outside \{2, 3\} the traceless centralizer \mathrm{diag}(y_2, y_2, y_3, y_3, y_3) satisfies 2 y_2 + 3 y_3 = 0 if and only if y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3} y_2. Fixing the doublet normalisation y_2 = 1 pins y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}, gives the exterior-pair quark doublet in V_2 \otimes W_3^* hypercharge y_2 + y_3 = +\tfrac{1}{3}, and yields the Killing traces \mathrm{tr}(T_3^2) = \tfrac{1}{2} and \mathrm{tr}((Y_F/2)^2) = \tfrac{5}{6}, hence the unrenormalized Weinberg ratio \mathrm{tr}(T_3^2)/(\mathrm{tr}(T_3^2) + \mathrm{tr}((Y_F/2)^2)) = \tfrac{3}{8}. On single strands, combining the weak-crossing sign s_2 \in \{\pm 1\} with the W_3 versus W_3^* triality orientation \tau_3 \in \{\pm 1\} via Q = \tfrac{1}{2} s_2 + \tfrac{1}{6} \tau_3 reproduces (+\tfrac{2}{3}, -\tfrac{1}{3}, +\tfrac{1}{3}, -\tfrac{2}{3}) on (u, d, \bar d, \bar u) and separates \bar u (-\tfrac{2}{3}) from d (-\tfrac{1}{3}) by +\tfrac{1}{3} \neq 0 despite their identical crossing sign -1. This implication is proved conditionally on W_3^*: constructing W_3 categorically in the multi-fibre groupoid remains the open antecedent.
